How Vector Search Works

Vector search finds documents by meaning instead of by exact words. Each document is turned into a list of numbers called an embedding, and documents with similar meaning end up close to each other in that space.

To answer a query, the system embeds the query text with the same model and then looks for the stored vectors that are nearest to it. Cosine similarity is the most common way to measure how close two vectors are.

For small collections an exact scan over every vector is fast enough. Approximate indexes such as HNSW only become necessary when the collection grows to millions of vectors and exact search becomes too slow.

Long documents are usually split into chunks before they are embedded, because embedding models have a limited input length and because smaller passages give more precise matches.
